correctness.rationale: Away from the measure-zero exceptional offsets, section vertices correspond bijectively to crossed edges. The upper Boolean halfspace A has size at most 2^(n−1) by antipodality, and cube edge isoperimetry (or the stated layer induction with the binary entropy chord bound) gives |A|≤V≤n|A|. For iid Gaussian coefficients the conditioned orientation multiplies the angular density by W_n/||G||₂. After dividing by √n this weight is bounded by one and converges almost surely to μ, giving total-variation convergence of the normalized tilt to one. The uniform absolute relative offset remains independent. For almost every sequence of magnitudes, the empirical log-cosh transform converges locally uniformly by the strong law and the Lipschitz bound. Chernoff gives the upper rate; at any b>a tilt by the unique λ with Λ′(λ)=b, use variance ≤ΣG_i²/n² to concentrate, then shrink the interval about b and let b decrease to a. Squeezing at fixed thresholds handles uW_n/n→μu; monotonicity and rational thresholds yield a common full-measure set for the coupled offset. Thus this is a weak limit under affine sampling, with a quenched sign-tail step, not a fixed-offset annealed LDP. Strict increase of I yields the stated CDF. At zero I(x)=x²/2+O(x⁴). At the other end put h=μ(1−u) and K=μπ²/24; the variational expression for Y is inf_λ[hλ+K/λ+O(λ⁻³)] in the large-λ regime. The minimizing λ is of order h^(−1/2), by bounding the positive correction above and below by constants times 1/λ and comparing with λ=√(K/h). This gives 2√(Kh)+O(h^(3/2)); inversion gives the stated 3/π and √π with the stated remainder orders. Direct offset integration gives the known 2^(n−1) mean. Weak convergence and absence of an atom at log 2 imply V/2^(n−1)→0 in probability by bounding each exceedance with an upper tail below log 2 and then sending that tail to the endpoint. The frozen script was inspected, not executed; an independent half-normal quadrature and bisection give λ≈0.4757198357 and median 0.606413254948, consistent with the stated numerical value.
